panels.description: Instance CPU. On burstable classes sustained load above the baseline spends credits (next row).
panels.title: CPU Utilization

panels.description: Memory the OS could reclaim. A steady decline with rising swap is the signal to size up.
panels.title: Freeable Memory

panels.description: Free space on the data volume. With storage autoscaling enabled this steps up when RDS grows the volume.
panels.title: Free Storage

panels.description: Burstable-class credits. A falling balance means load is above the baseline; any surplus balance means burst is being billed (unlimited mode) or will be throttled (standard mode).
panels.title: CPU Credits

panels.description: Open client connections. The API's pool section above shows who holds them.
panels.title: Connections

panels.description: Swap in use. Growth here with falling freeable memory means the instance is memory-bound.

panels.description: Data-node CPU.
panels.title: CPU Utilization

panels.description: Share of the Java heap in use. A sawtooth is normal garbage collection; what matters is the floor it returns to. Sustained time above 80% means the heap is too small; the circuit breaker trips near 95%.
panels.title: JVM Memory Pressure

panels.description: Used ÷ (used + free) across the domain, derived from the two CloudWatch space metrics. Lines mark the shard-allocation watermarks: low 85% (no new shards), high 90% (shards relocate), flood 95% (indices go read-only).
panels.title: Storage Used

panels.description: Search requests per minute across all shards.
panels.title: Search Rate

panels.description: Time a shard spends completing a search request.
panels.title: Search Latency

panels.description: Documents across all indices in the domain.
panels.title: Searchable Documents

panels.description: Indexing requests per minute.
panels.title: Indexing Rate

panels.description: Time a shard spends completing an indexing request.
panels.title: Indexing Latency

panels.description: EBS write bytes per second on the data nodes.
panels.title: Write Throughput

panels.description: KNNGraphMemoryUsage is already in KiB (CloudWatch reports the k-NN native cache in KB). Residency, not storage: it rises when segments are queried and reads 0 when nothing has been. Lines: 70% of the measured 4,601,500 KiB budget, and the ceiling.
panels.title: KNN Memory Usage

panels.description: Queries served from k-NN graphs already resident in the native cache. Hits against a flat memory line mean the working set fits.
panels.title: KNN Cache Hits

panels.description: Signs the native cache is too small for the vector working set. All four should sit at zero; evictions are the first to move.
panels.title: KNN Pressure Events

panels.description: EBS operations per second on the data nodes.
panels.title: Read / Write IOPS

panels.description: Responses per minute by status class, stacked.
panels.title: HTTP Responses / min

panels.description: Worst cluster health seen in each minute. Yellow means a replica shard is unassigned; red means a primary is.
panels.title: Cluster Status

panels.description: Host CPU and the single engine thread. On nodes with few vCPUs the engine thread saturates long before the host figure looks busy.
panels.title: CPU Utilization

panels.description: Dataset as a share of the node's usable memory. Evictions begin when it hits the maxmemory policy's limit.
panels.title: Memory Utilization

panels.description: Memory held by the dataset.
panels.title: Bytes Used

panels.description: Burstable-class credits; a falling balance means load is above the baseline.
panels.title: CPU Credit Balance

panels.description: Open client connections, and new connections per period. A climbing new-connection count with flat current connections means clients are not pooling.
panels.title: Connections

panels.description: Swap in use on the node. Should stay flat and small.
panels.title: Swap Usage

panels.description: Keys evicted per period to stay under maxmemory. Non-zero means the dataset no longer fits.
panels.title: Evictions

panels.description: Hits ÷ (hits + misses) per period. Gaps are periods with no reads at all.
panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio

panels.description: Network bytes per second in and out of the node.
panels.title: Network Throughput
